name: Prepare a construction management, design-build or IPD proposal
summary: Public institutions and private owners who want the contractor involved before design is finished pick a construction manager, design-builder or IPD partner through a request for proposals instead of a lump-sum tender. The business development manager runs a team of a proposal coordinator, preconstruction manager, estimator, scheduler and the proposed site leaders to write the approach, price the fee and general conditions, and for design-build add a design team and a priced concept. Executive approval, surety letters and a final compliance check come in the last days before closing, and shortlisted firms then rehearse and attend an interview. The work is slow because it competes with live projects for the same senior people, and it is error-prone because page limits, mandatory forms and two-envelope rules make small mistakes disqualifying.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor with about $1.5B annual revenue, central business development and preconstruction staff, and regional operations offices that supply the proposed project teams.
baseline.notes: Describes negotiated and best-value pursuits in 2019-2022, mostly under CCDC 5A/5B construction management, some design-build and a few IPD (CCDC 30) pursuits.

unit_of_work: one proposal (CM, design-build or IPD) from receipt of the RFP to the owner's award or regret
trigger: The opportunity pipeline passes on an owner's RFP that the company has decided to pursue.
end_state: The owner has awarded the contract and the file is with the contract award team, or the pursuit is closed after a no-go, withdrawal or loss with debrief notes in the CRM.

volume.seasonality: More public-sector RFPs in late winter and spring as owners commit capital budgets before fiscal year-end; fewer in July, August and December.

evidence.note: Organisation file volume kept; consistent with about 10 project starts a month of which a minority are negotiated.

surge.cause: Spring release of public capital projects after budgets are approved

evidence.note: Author's estimate from the timing of provincial and institutional capital approvals.

systems.name: Public tender and bid portals (MERX, Bids&Tenders, Biddingo, provincial portals)
Take-off and estimating software with Excel bid sheets
CPM scheduling software (Primavera P6, Microsoft Project)
Reporting and dashboards (Excel cost reports, Power BI)

steps.name: Log RFP and open pursuit file
steps.description: The proposal coordinator downloads the RFP and addenda from the bid portal or the owner's email, records the opportunity stage in the CRM, opens a pursuit folder and builds a compliance matrix listing every mandatory form, page limit, rated criterion and deadline.

error.defect_description: A mandatory form, page limit or addendum is missed in the compliance matrix.

evidence.note: The NCC RFP shows the mandatory requirements, page limits and rated criteria that a compliance matrix has to track; touch time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hold go or no-go review of the full RFP
steps.description: The business development manager reads the full RFP, contract form and evaluation scheme and meets the VP, a preconstruction manager and an operations manager to confirm fit, competition, staff availability, fee expectations and bonding before committing proposal effort. A no-go is recorded in the CRM with the reason.

next.condition: no-go after reading the full RFP

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Commit proposed project team
steps.description: The operations manager checks the staffing plan for the project manager, superintendent and project estimator who can start on the owner's dates, confirms their names for the proposal and releases them for resumes and interview preparation.

error.defect_description: A named person is later committed to another project and must be replaced before award.

evidence.note: Owners rate the proposed project manager, estimator and superintendent (OAA) and key individuals carry most technical points (NCC); durations are estimates.

steps.name: Review form of contract and supplementary conditions
steps.description: Contracts counsel reads the owner's CCDC 5A, 5B, 14 or 30 form and supplementary conditions, marks liability caps, liquidated damages, GMP conversion terms and indemnities, and writes the list of exceptions or clarifications the proposal may carry.

control.basis: Corporate contract review policy: legal review of non-standard contract terms before any proposal is submitted

evidence.note: CCDC 5A/5B fee and GMP options described by the OAA; review effort is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft proposal narrative and resumes
steps.description: The proposal coordinator assembles corporate experience, project sheets, safety statistics and tailored resumes from the marketing library, writes the first draft of each rated section within the page limits and circulates it to section authors.

error.defect_description: Project sheets or resumes do not match the rated criteria or exceed page limits.

evidence.note: Rated sections with page limits and minimum scores follow the NCC RFP; hours are estimates.

steps.name: Write preconstruction and management approach
steps.description: The preconstruction manager writes the approach to design-phase cost control, estimate stages, value engineering, trade packaging and early works, and the risk register for the project, drawing on comparable past projects.

evidence.note: Preconstruction services content (cost estimates at each design phase, constructability, scheduling, trade packages) from the OAA practice tip; hours are estimates.

steps.name: Prepare proposal schedule
steps.description: The scheduler builds a summary CPM schedule covering design stages, preconstruction, permits, trade package tendering, construction phases and turnover, and writes the schedule narrative the RFP asks for.

error.defect_description: Durations are not tied to the owner's funding or occupancy dates.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Estimate general conditions, staffing cost and fee
steps.description: The estimator prices the site staff loaded against the schedule, site general requirements, insurance and bonding, and sets the preconstruction fee and construction fee in the form the RFP asks for (lump sum, hourly rates or percentage).

error.defect_description: Staff durations or rates do not match the schedule, or an item is carried in both fee and general conditions.

next.condition: design-build or IPD proposal that needs a design team and a priced concept
construction management proposal priced on fee and general conditions

evidence.note: Fee forms from CCDC 5A/5B (OAA); price envelope scored separately (NCC); the 30% design-build share is an estimate.

steps.name: Engage design consultants for the design-build team
steps.description: The design manager invites two or three architectural firms, agrees pursuit fees, scope and teaming terms, and sets the concept design deliverables against the owner's statement of requirements.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Wait for consultants' concept design
steps.description: The design team produces concept plans, outline specifications and a basis of design to the owner's requirements while the design manager attends weekly design meetings; the contractor cannot price until drawings arrive.

error.defect_description: Concept omits owner requirements that later need redesign.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Price the concept design with trade input
steps.description: The estimator takes off quantities from the concept, sends mechanical, electrical and envelope packages to trades through trade tendering for budget prices, levels the replies and builds the design-build price with design fees and contingency.

error.defect_description: Quantities or scope missed because the concept is incomplete.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Chief estimator reviews price and fee
steps.description: The chief estimator compares the fee, general conditions, contingency and design-build price with recent wins and losses in the cost database and returns the estimate with comments when assumptions look wrong.

control.basis: Estimating department review policy: senior estimator review of every priced submission

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Prepare bid summary for executive approval
steps.description: The business development manager writes a two-page summary of the fee, margin, contract exceptions, staffing, competition and risks and attaches it to the approval request.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Obtain executive bid approval
steps.description: The VP of business development approves within delegated limits or takes the summary to the executive bid approval meeting for large projects, unusual contract terms or thin fees, and records conditions such as a higher fee or fewer exceptions.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: executive bid approval above a contract value or for non-standard terms

next.condition: approved subject to a fee or staffing change

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Obtain surety letter or bid security
steps.description: The treasury manager asks the surety broker for the consent-of-surety or bonding capacity letter the RFP requires and files it with the submission forms.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Assemble and produce final submission
steps.description: The proposal coordinator merges the final sections, applies the layout, checks page counts, completes and signs the forms, and prepares the technical and price files as separate submissions where the RFP uses two envelopes.

error.defect_description: A form unsigned, pages over the limit or price shown in the technical file.

evidence.note: Two-envelope submission and page limits from the NCC RFP; hours are estimates.

steps.name: Final compliance review and sign-off
steps.description: The VP reads the proposal against the compliance matrix and the approval conditions, checks that the fee matches the approval and signs the submission letter, or returns it for corrections.

control.basis: Signing authority: proposals and price forms signed by an officer of the company

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Submit proposal before closing
steps.description: The proposal coordinator uploads or emails the technical and price files before the closing time, keeps the time-stamped receipt and records the submission in the CRM.

error.defect_description: Late or incomplete upload makes the proposal non-compliant.

evidence.note: Closing date and time, email submission and late proposals disqualified, from the NCC RFP.

steps.name: Wait for owner's technical evaluation
steps.description: The owner's evaluation committee scores the technical proposals against the rated criteria and minimum scores, calls references and decides which proponents to interview or whether to open price envelopes directly.

next.condition: below the technical threshold or not shortlisted

evidence.note: Minimum points per criterion, reference forms within 5 business days and price opened only for compliant proposals (NCC); shortlist share is an estimate.

steps.name: Organise and rehearse the interview
steps.description: The business development manager builds the interview plan and slides, assigns topics to the proposed project manager, superintendent and preconstruction manager, and runs two or three rehearsals with likely owner questions.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Proposed project manager prepares interview part
steps.description: The proposed project manager studies the drawings and site, prepares the logistics, phasing and schedule talking points, and joins the rehearsals so the owner meets the person who will run the job.

evidence.note: Owners consider the proposed project manager, estimator and superintendent when selecting a CM (OAA); hours are estimates.

steps.name: Travel to the owner's interview
steps.description: The interview team drives or flies to the owner's office or campus, often another city served by a regional office, and returns the same day.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Present at the owner interview
steps.description: The business development manager leads a 60 to 90 minute presentation and question session with the owner's committee and consultant, and the team answers questions on fee, staffing, schedule and approach.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Wait for owner's decision
steps.description: The owner combines technical, interview and price scores, may ask for fee clarifications, and obtains internal or board approval before issuing a notice of award or a regret letter.

evidence.note: Technical 70% / price 30% scoring after a technical threshold (NCC); win share after interview is an estimate.

steps.name: Record award and hand over to contract award
steps.description: The business development manager updates the CRM, informs the team, and passes the proposal, fee forms and exceptions list to the contract award team for negotiation of the CM agreement.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Request debrief and record the loss
steps.description: The business development manager requests a debrief, attends it with the team, records scores, winning fee range and lessons in the CRM, and closes the pursuit file.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

exceptions.name: Design-build concept pricing
exceptions.description: Design-build and some IPD proposals need a design team and a priced concept, which adds two to six weeks and most of the estimating hours.

exceptions.name: Executive sends price back
exceptions.description: The executive approval meeting asks for a higher fee or a leaner staffing plan, so the estimator reprices in the last days before closing.

exceptions.name: Late compliance correction
exceptions.description: The final review finds an unsigned form, page overrun or price in the technical file, and the coordinator reworks the package on closing day.

exceptions.name: No interview
exceptions.description: Some owners score written proposals and price only, so the team goes straight from submission to the decision.

evidence.note: Built from a 38-day RFP period (NCC AL1821: issued 12 March, closed 19 April 2021) plus the author's estimate of 3 to 8 weeks for evaluation, interview and owner approval.

pain_points.description: Proposal effort competes with live projects for the same project managers, superintendents and preconstruction managers, so sections wait and interview rehearsals get squeezed.

evidence.note: Owners rate the proposed project manager, estimator and superintendent, so these people must write and present.

pain_points.description: Executive approval and surety letters arrive in the last days before closing and any change to the fee forces repricing under deadline pressure.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from how executive bid reviews are scheduled close to closing dates; the organisation file describes the same pattern for bid approval.

pain_points.description: Strict page limits, mandatory forms and separate price envelopes mean a small assembly error can make a strong proposal non-compliant.

evidence.note: Pages over the limit are not evaluated, minimum scores per criterion and late proposals disqualified.

pain_points.description: Design-build concepts depend on outside architects working on pursuit fees, so pricing waits for drawings and is done on incomplete information.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common design-build pursuit practice in Canada.

sources.title: Request for Proposal: Construction Management Services, Solicitation AL1821
sources.supports: A 2021 Canadian public CM services RFP: tender file dated 12 March 2021 and closing 19 April 2021 (38 days); two-envelope submission with technical proposal by email 1 and price proposal by email 2; minimum points required on each rated criterion before price is opened; technical 70% and price 30%; page limits per rated criterion; key individuals rated on qualifications; client reference forms to be returned within 5 business days of request; price proposal irrevocable for 180 days; questions due 14 calendar days before closing.

sources.title: Practice Tip PT.23.2: CCDC Construction Management Contracts (version 2.1)
sources.supports: CCDC 5A (CM for services) and CCDC 5B (CM for services and construction) and CCDC 17 for trade contractors; the CM is engaged during design for constructability, estimated construction costs and scheduling; work is packaged and bid by individual trades; the CM fee may be a stipulated amount, hourly rates or a percentage of the cost of the work, with options under 5B to move to a guaranteed maximum price or stipulated price later; owners selecting a CM by RFP consider the experience of the proposed project manager, estimator and superintendent; the 2010 forms were the ones in use until the 2025 editions.

assumptions: The process starts after the opportunity pipeline's pursue decision and ends at award or loss; negotiating the CM agreement is the contract award process.
Loaded costs and titles come from the organisation file (wage x 1.35 for salaried staff).
Roles not listed for this process in the organisation file but needed here: estimator, chief-estimator, scheduler, project-manager, operations-manager, contracts-counsel and treasury-manager.
The executive approval meeting is modelled as one approval step by the VP of business development; the executive bid approval process holds the detail.
Win rate overall is about 0.55 x 0.42 + 0.1 x 0.42, roughly 27% of submitted proposals; this is an estimate for negotiated work, not a published figure.
Mix of 70% CM proposals priced on fee and general conditions and 30% design-build or IPD proposals needing a priced concept is an estimate.
Step times are sequential in the simulation; steps marked concurrent run in parallel in practice, so the simulated cycle slightly overstates the elapsed time of the drafting stage.
